author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader can filter the veterinarian directory by specialty through the URL
summary: The directory page and the reinstated machine-readable list accept an optional specialty query parameter that narrows them to veterinarians holding that specialty. Matching is whole-name and case-insensitive. Without a usable value, both surfaces behave as today.
acceptance_criteria: GET /vets.html?specialty=<name> lists only veterinarians holding that specialty, and pagination applies to the filtered list.
GET /vets?specialty=<name> returns only veterinarians holding that specialty.
Every pagination link on a filtered page carries the specialty, so filtered pages stay navigable.
Matching is on the whole specialty name and case-insensitive on both surfaces: a differently cased name matches, a prefix does not.
A specialty no veterinarian holds yields HTTP 200 with the normal page or JSON document and an empty veterinarian list.
An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if the parameter were absent on both surfaces, and pagination links then omit the parameter.
Without the parameter both endpoints behave as today; /vets returns every veterinarian.
Neither surface gains a form, dropdown, or other page control.

PRD edge cases 2 to 8 of Veterinarian directory hold: no paging on the JSON list; a match keeps every specialty shown; surrounding spaces are not stripped; link values survive unchanged and are treated as plain text; blank values leave links bare; a page past the end behaves as on the unfiltered directory; case-insensitivity holds on every supported database.
non_goals: A form, dropdown, or other page control on either surface (NG-10); a visible control may come as a follow-up request.
Filtering by any attribute other than specialty.
Paging the JSON list, or any other change to /vets beyond the filter.
Reusing or reinstating the id REQ-VET-002.
notes: Fresh requirement: REQ-VET-003 is the requirement the owner asked to mint for the JSON surface, and it carries the filter on both surfaces; REQ-VET-001 is unchanged. Slice size: one behavior under one matching contract, with code as the single primary surface. The HTML and JSON routes stay together because the owner defines them as one contract. Open questions, recorded in the PRD and taken at the narrowest reading: spaces around a non-blank value are not stripped; a repeated specialty parameter has no defined behavior and needs no test. Design-owned follow-through: the PRD no longer calls the second route a defect, so the system-design Known Defects row saying it serves no requirement and the VetController row (REQ-VET-001 only) need aligning. The new non-goal ADR needs its row in the docs/adr/README.md index, which is outside the product expert's write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays in the vet feature package and follows the paged repository query of owner search (OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith, grep-resolved; the IDE oracle is not connected). New ground: a request-derived value meets the unbounded vets cache and three vendors that compare specialty names differently, so docs/system-design.md gains § Scale and Load, a Persistence paragraph, and two Threat Model rows, and a new ADR records the query form. Placement: the matching rule lives in VetRepository as one uncached query; VetController holds only the blank-value normalization, which the Web controller row in docs/architecture-principles.md classes as binding. Vets, Vet, Specialty, VetRepository, and VetController rows now carry REQ-VET-003. The Known Defects row on the machine-readable route is removed, since the route now serves a requirement.
integration_points: Binding: both handlers bind specialty as a request-scoped String through @RequestParam(required = false). No persisted type is bound, so no new @InitBinder is needed.

Repository query: one method, findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable), returning Page<Vet>, with no @Cacheable. Distinct is required because the schemas do not make specialty names unique. The page surface passes PageRequest.of(page - 1, 5, Sort.by("id")); the JSON surface passes Pageable.unpaged(Sort.by("id")) and adds the content to Vets. Never join-fetch specialties: the mapped EAGER load must keep every specialty on a match (PRD edge case 3).

Absent path: a null or String.isBlank value calls exactly today's cached findAll(Pageable) and findAll(), with the existing unsorted PageRequest. A non-blank value is passed unchanged, never stripped.

Model and template: the handler adds a specialty attribute, null when blank. vetList.html appends it to all five link kinds (numbered, first, previous, next, last) through one definition, a th:with on the pagination div building an empty string or '&specialty=' + ${#uris.escapeQueryParam(specialty)}. A null value passed as a Thymeleaf link parameter is not an acceptable omission; prove the bare link in the omit test. Add no form, dropdown, or message key.
Boundary double, framework transport: real MockMvc in VetControllerTests, driving real binding and template rendering.

Boundary double, repository in VetControllerTests: the class's existing @MockitoBean VetRepository, a framework stub because @WebMvcTest loads no repository. It proves routing, normalization, passed arguments, and link rendering only. It may not carry a matching test name.

Boundary double, repository for the matching rule: real repositories on a real store, no double. PetClinicIntegrationTests hosts the surface matching, prefix, unknown-specialty, unstripped-value, and every-specialty-kept names over HTTP against seeded H2 data. theSpecialtyFilterShouldIgnoreLetterCaseOnEveryDatabase runs in PetClinicIntegrationTests, MySqlIntegrationTests, and PostgresIntegrationTests against the real VetRepository.

Filtered paging on a real store: seed data holds at most two veterinarians per specialty, under the page size of five. ClinicServiceTests drives the query with a page size of one over surgery to prove page content and totals; VetControllerTests covers the multi-page links with a stubbed PageImpl.

patterns.description: processFindForm and findPaginatedForOwnersLastName: paged repository query with the pagination model; the shape to follow, except that it strips its value and this slice must not.
The decision behind the uncached query and the rejected alternatives.

risks.risk: Specialty filter path, § Scale and Load row 'Specialty filter, both surfaces': caching the method makes each distinct value a retained entry in the vets cache, which has no size limit or expiry.
risks.mitigation: No @Cacheable on the filter method; Threat Model row 'Memory exhaustion through request-supplied cache keys'. Simplest readable form: one query per request.

risks.risk: Letter case: a plain equality passes on MySQL alone, since H2 and PostgreSQL compare specialty names case-sensitively (docs/system-design.md § Persistence).
risks.mitigation: IgnoreCase folds both operands in the query; prove it on each vendor. A stubbed repository proves nothing here.

risks.risk: Template expression injection: routing the value through the template's existing __${...}__ link style evaluates request text as an expression.
risks.mitigation: Threat Model row 'Template expression injection through pagination links': encoded query value only, never preprocessing. Keep __ only on the integer page values already there.

risks.risk: Reserved characters in links: an unencoded value breaks on '&', '+', '%', and spaces (PRD edge case 5).
risks.mitigation: #uris.escapeQueryParam, proved by theVetListPaginationLinksShouldKeepSpacesAndReservedCharactersInTheSpecialtyAsPlainText, which must assert the decoded value survives.

risks.risk: Paging order: a DISTINCT query with no order can repeat or drop rows across pages.
risks.mitigation: Sort.by("id") on the filtered path only; the unfiltered path stays unchanged. Row 'Specialty filter, both surfaces'.

risks.risk: Page past the end (PRD edge case 7): a separate branch or clamp would diverge from the unfiltered directory.
risks.mitigation: Share addPaginationModel and the template; add no filtered-only page handling.

risks.risk: A NUL character in the value (%00) is expected to fail on the PostgreSQL driver and return the error page rather than an empty list. Unverified. Owner search carries the same baseline, per docs/security-principles.md § Applying this section.
risks.mitigation: No handling in this slice; recorded for the owner, since the PRD names no such value. Add a test only if a reviewer requires the 200 contract for it.

notes: Follow-through from the prd-entry is done: the Known Defects row is removed, the VetController row is aligned, and docs/adr/README.md carries the index row for the non-goal ADR plus the new ADR. docs/system-design.md had no § Scale and Load, though the harness template requires it, so it was added with the directory's rows only. The vet row size is written as unrecorded, treated as bounded; the owner corrects it if the figure is known. Open for the owner: on MySQL the default collation also disregards accents, so an accented variant matches there and not on H2 or PostgreSQL; no requirement covers it. A repeated specialty parameter reaches the handler as Spring's comma-joined String and matches nothing; PRD Open Questions leave it undefined and no code or test should address it. The test_names are used verbatim, placed per integration_points. docs/security-principles.md is outside this agent's write scope; the two new threats sit in the docs/system-design.md Threat Model, which reviewers read. No design-doc-autofix records existed to audit.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader can filter the veterinarian directory by specialty through the URL
summary: The directory page and the reinstated machine-readable list accept an optional specialty query parameter that narrows them to veterinarians holding that specialty. Matching is whole-name and case-insensitive. Without a usable value, both surfaces behave as today.
acceptance_criteria: GET /vets.html?specialty=<name> lists only veterinarians holding that specialty, and pagination applies to the filtered list.
GET /vets?specialty=<name> returns only veterinarians holding that specialty.
Every pagination link on a filtered page carries the specialty, so filtered pages stay navigable.
Matching is on the whole specialty name and case-insensitive on both surfaces: a differently cased name matches, a prefix does not.
A specialty no veterinarian holds yields HTTP 200 with the normal page or JSON document and an empty veterinarian list.
An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if the parameter were absent on both surfaces, and pagination links then omit the parameter.
Without the parameter both endpoints behave as today; /vets returns every veterinarian.
Neither surface gains a form, dropdown, or other page control.

PRD edge cases 2 to 8 of Veterinarian directory hold: no paging on the JSON list; a match keeps every specialty shown; surrounding spaces are not stripped; link values survive unchanged and are treated as plain text; blank values leave links bare; a page past the end behaves as on the unfiltered directory; case-insensitivity holds on every supported database.
non_goals: A form, dropdown, or other page control on either surface (NG-10); a visible control may come as a follow-up request.
Filtering by any attribute other than specialty.
Paging the JSON list, or any other change to /vets beyond the filter.
Reusing or reinstating the id REQ-VET-002.
